analysis.title: Is the case for Europe broadening?
key_insights: Europe has outperformed during the US AI unwind. Since 6 October the STOXX 600 is up 3.3% while the S&P 500 is down 5.2%, the Nasdaq 100 down 12.9% and the SOX down more than 27%. Pictet asks whether this is more than a defensive rotation away from US semiconductors.

Pictet says history sets a high bar. Past European relative rallies came as US growth leadership weakened, but cheap valuations alone rarely produced lasting regional leadership. Durable phases coincided with improving European earnings revisions, stronger domestic growth, supportive currencies and a narrowing US growth premium.

NVIDIA reported after the close on 17 November. Q3 revenue was USD 115.8bn, up 103% y/y. Adjusted EPS was USD 2.68 against USD 2.48 expected. Q4 revenue guidance is USD 130bn. Pictet frames the print as a possible clearing event for US tech.
Pictet flags continuing leadership uncertainty at NVIDIA after Jensen Huang's recent resignation. It calls the Anthropic IPO a further test of appetite for the AI theme.

Pictet's scenario map: a strong NVIDIA result and an over-subscribed Anthropic IPO could revive US tech leadership. A disappointment or continued execution uncertainty could reinforce Europe's near-term appeal. The more informative signal would be European outperformance continuing while US tech stabilises.

The Nasdaq 100 closed below its 200-day moving average on 13 November and is more than 13% below its 6 October all-time high. Over the rolling 20 trading days the Nasdaq 100 is down 7.8% and the STOXX Europe 600 is up 3.7%.

Sector mix: Information Technology is 35.3% of the S&P 500. Financials and Industrials together are 43.6% of the STOXX Europe 600, with Health Care at 13.6% and Consumer Staples at 8.6%. Pictet says this mix is a counterweight to AI weakness but does not insulate Europe from a broad sell-off.

Banks led the first leg of European cyclical outperformance versus the US but their relative momentum has consolidated. Industrials are now turning higher against US peers. A handover from defensives to Banks and Industrials would make the Europe trade less dependent on US tech weakness.

EUR/USD reversed from resistance near 1.2020, which coincides with the 200-month SMA, and is approaching 1.0930. That level is the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement of the advance from April 2025 and the lower bound of its short-term range. A sustained break below could expose 1.0650, and the RSI has broken below support.

Pictet argues a weaker euro could lift European earnings through translation of overseas revenue and export competitiveness, mainly for Industrials and Health Care. The US-Europe earnings revision ratio spread has narrowed to 1.8%, with the US at 14.2% and Europe at 12.3%. EUR/USD is down 5.3% y/y.

European banks rebounded in November, with the MSCI Europe Banks index up 6.5% month to date on resilient Q3 earnings, revenue growth, cost discipline and moderate loan-loss provisions. The index is still down 2.4% relative to the broader MSCI benchmark over the past month. Higher German two-year yields could support net interest income.

The German 10-year yield pulled back from its 3.66% wave-3 target to around 3.27%, below its 50-day SMA. Support sits at 3.03% to 3.10%, reinforced by the rising 200-day SMA. A move above 3.66% would put 4.21% back in play, and a break below 3.03% would weaken the breakout structure.

Pictet's Exposure Optimisation Model suggests 71% exposure for Europe against 38% for the US. The gap widened as US suggested exposure fell. The model's Europe signals are very bullish on regime and valuation despite weaker economic readings.

Macro is a constraint. The Citi Economic Surprise Index for the eurozone is at -7.5 against +63.9 for the US. The European Commission projects euro-area GDP growth of 1.2% in 2026 and 2027, with 2026 inflation at 3.2%. This year's growth was supported by exports while investment was weaker than expected.

The SMI hit a record 15,272 and is retreating, possibly ending a Wave 3 move. Support is 14,720 to 14,380, with 16,300 as the next potential target. RSI shows bearish divergence, which supports a near-term pause.

sector_views.rationale: Banks rebounded in November and German yields may support net interest income. Relative momentum has consolidated, the index still lags the broader MSCI benchmark over the past month, and a prior Pictet note argued for selectivity.
Relative trend against US peers is turning higher and a weaker euro helps exporters. Pictet presents this as a possible signal of cyclical broadening.
Defensive exposure at 13.6% of the STOXX 600, with a weaker euro helping pharmaceutical exporters. EUR 366bn of EU pharma exports in 2025, 43.8% to the US.
At 35.3% of the S&P 500 it is the focus of AI capex and financing concerns. NVIDIA's results may or may not clear the sector, and Pictet makes no explicit call.

earnings_insights: NVIDIA, reported after the close on 17 November: Q3 revenue USD 115.8bn reported, up 103% y/y. Adjusted EPS USD 2.68 reported against USD 2.48 consensus expected. Q4 revenue guidance USD 130bn (company guidance).
European banks: Q3 earnings were resilient, with revenue growth, cost discipline and moderate loan-loss provisions cited as drivers of the November rebound.
Earnings revision ratio (ERR): US 14.2% and Europe 12.3%, with the US-Europe spread narrowed to 1.8%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A softer run of data against expectations than the US, though not a contraction in Europe.
US data is beating expectations by a wide margin, a contrast with the eurozone.

macro_indicators.indicator: Euro-area real GDP growth (European Commission Autumn 2026 forecast)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Pictet reads this as subdued underlying growth, a constraint on the Europe case.
Renewed inflation pressure is a potential constraint on Europe's diversification appeal.
Pulled back from the 3.66% target but above 3.03% to 3.10% support, which keeps the medium-term uptrend intact.
A weaker euro supports European exporters' earnings. Technical support is at 1.0930, then 1.0650.

risk_factors: A broad market sell-off, which Europe's sector mix cannot insulate against.
A strong NVIDIA result and an over-subscribed Anthropic IPO reviving US tech leadership and ending Europe's relative strength.
Weak eurozone economic surprises, subdued growth, renewed inflation and tighter financing conditions.
Leadership uncertainty at NVIDIA after Jensen Huang's recent resignation.
A break below 1.0930 on EUR/USD, which could expose 1.0650.
A break below 3.03% on the German 10-year yield, which would weaken the breakout structure.
SMI consolidation after a record high, with bearish RSI divergence.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower valuations, less AI capex reliance, a sector mix weighted to Financials and Industrials, a weaker euro and a rebound in banks could make the outperformance broader than a tactical move away from US tech. Pictet's EOM suggests 71% exposure for Europe against 38% for the US.
tension_points.bear_case: Eurozone economic surprises are at -7.5 against +63.9 for the US, euro-area growth is projected at 1.2%, and inflation is 3.2%. Cheap valuations alone have rarely produced sustained regional leadership. A strong NVIDIA result and an over-subscribed Anthropic IPO could revive US tech leadership.
tension_points.what_invalidates: European relative strength fading once US tech stabilises after the NVIDIA print and the Anthropic IPO. Pictet treats continued European outperformance during US tech stabilisation as the confirming signal.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher German two-year yields can lift net interest income where loans reprice faster than deposits. Banks are up 6.5% in November on resilient Q3 earnings, cost discipline and moderate provisions.
tension_points.bear_case: The banks index is still down 2.4% relative to the broader MSCI benchmark over the past month, relative momentum has consolidated, and the German 10-year yield has pulled back from its 3.66% target.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the German 10-year yield below 3.03%, which would weaken the breakout structure and the Elliott wave count.

theme_stances.evidence: the case for Europe looks broader than simply avoiding US technology

theme_stances.key_argument: A weaker euro could lift earnings of Europe's internationally exposed Industrials and Health Care sectors.
theme_stances.evidence: A weaker euro could support European earnings through the translation of overseas revenues
